text:
RESULTS: MRI_Brain_with_contrast: No mass lesions, no hydrocephalus, no signs of increased intracranial pressure, and no vascular malformations identified.

MRI_Brain_slices: Axial, Coronal, and Sagittal T1-weighted images with contrast show no focal abnormalities. The ventricular system is normal in size and shape. There is no evidence of mass effect, midline shift, or acute hemorrhage. The visual pathway structures appear intact.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI results are puzzling; they rule out space-occupying lesions and increased intracranial pressure, yet your exam showed papilledema and visual field loss. speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Visual Evoked Potentials: Prolonged P100 latency and reduced amplitude, consistent with optic pathway compression or demyelination.

speaker: Doctor
text: The visual evoked potentials suggest pathology along the optic pathways despite a normal MRI; given your age and the subacute progression of headache, worsening vision, and papilledema, have you noticed any subtle cognitive decline or memory issues? speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lumbar Puncture: Opening pressure is elevated at 32 cm H2O. CSF analysis reveals no pleocytosis, normal protein levels, and normal glucose. Cytology is negative for malignant cells.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated opening pressure of 32 cm H2O with normal CSF composition and a negative MRI for mass effect or hydrocephalus is highly characteristic of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension.
